labels.notes: Read against benzecri1960_ch3.tex l.1142-1148 and l.795. remarque_somme_facettes_coniques (SommeFacettesConiques.lean:726) takes hL : DirectSum.IsInternal L (reading of « S(n) soit la somme des L_i », disclosed), hW : forall i, IsCorpsConvexeDans (L i) (W i) (strict convex part (IsConvexPart plus no antipodal pair, i.e. noyau vide, l.795), W i in l_i, closed, relInterior nonempty for the subspace topology of l_i: the paper's « corps convexe de L_i » with its parenthetical), and quantifies over every w with EstSommeS w W (§ 2 Déf. 5). The sum exists (estSommeS_sommeS), so that hypothesis is not vacuous. Conclusion: IsCorpsConvexeS n (closure w) (the strict lib's Déf. 11), and for every i, IsFacetteConique (closure w) (relInterior (L i) (W i)) (IsFacetteK plus noyau of the contingent = supportK, the strict Déf. 5), closure (relInterior) = W i, supportK = l_i. Under the three readings in the dispatch (E = ⊕ L_i, relative interior as the conical facette, corps convexe strict) Lean >= paper, for every p and every sum w, and the conclusion adds the closure and support facts. The relative-interior reading is forced: isFacetteK_iff_relInterior_eq proves W_i is literally a facette iff it equals its relative interior. The label is written without ** in the module docstring (l.10), and REPORT marks it partial with the readings stated: correct, because the conclusion is proved only in a reading.

instances: IsCorpsConvexeDans has a concrete Lean instance, isCorpsConvexeDans_blockW for any surjective f : Fin (n+1) -> I. It is used at f = id (vertices, blockW_id), at fArete = ![0,0,1] (closed edge plus vertex in S(2)) and at fArcs = ![0,0,1,1] (quarter arcs in S(3)). Each W_j is a genuine closed simplex block with a relative interior point, and nothing in it is degenerate. isInternal_blockL instantiates DirectSum.IsInternal. closure_somme_blockW instantiates the whole Remark, giving closure = TriangleInstance.simplexS n. relInterior, IsCore, proj, coneSomme, coneAppuiSomme and sommeS are definitions with no hypotheses to instantiate, and they are used in the instances.

findings_checked.notes: Hypotheses are satisfied (blockW fArete satisfies IsCorpsConvexeDans; EstSommeS w is satisfiable). Proves the closed edge blockW fArete 0 is not an IsFacetteK of closure w, while its relative interior is a conical facette of closure blockW fArete 0. Genuine against the literal wording « les W_i sont des facettes coniques », and it fails generically: for every W_i that is not a point, not only in a degenerate case. So it is not « imprecise » under the dispatch's degenerate-case criterion. It is better described as an abuse of language (a closed face named by its relatively open facette) whose intended form is proved for all p and all W_i. Not naming it not_ is defensible because the intended reading is evident and proved. The REPORT finding already says « false read literally ».

W = S(0) = univ, L = top, p = 1: it is IsConvexPart (insert 0 F = whole line, convex), closed, contained in l, with nonempty relative interior, so it satisfies the parenthetical alone. ofCone (kPrime univ) = univ is not IsCorpsConvexeS, and no w is an EstSommeS of it (F(univ) is not convex). This is a correct counterexample to the parenthetical-only reading. It is not a refutation of the Remark, because « corps convexe » (Déf. 11, l.795) includes noyau vide and the Lean carries it. « imprecise » (an incomplete parenthetical gloss) is the right word, and a non-not_ name is right.

findings.what: The literal-reading failure is called « imprecise rather than wrong ». It fails for every W_i that is not a point, not in a degenerate case only, so the dispatch's « imprecise » criterion (only a degenerate case fails) does not strictly apply. It is an abuse of language whose intended form is proved, and the finding text already says « false read literally ».
findings.fix: Word it as « false as printed (literal reading), an abuse of language whose evident intended form, relint W_i a conical facette of closure W_i, is proved », so that the /restate register (restate.py seed) picks it up and the author rules on it. No Lean change is needed.
